config_snapshot._purpose: exact tuning constants in effect this run, for reproducibility

source_weights._comment: Per-mention contribution. Higher = stronger signal. Tune by raising weights for sources you trust more.

convergence_multiplier._comment: When a topic appears in N or more DIFFERENT source types, score is multiplied. Counters monoculture (single-source loud day) and rewards cross-source agreement.

sector_config._comment: Dynamic sectors (radar quadrants) — recomputed every run based on what's actually active. Sectors carry over from yesterday's radar unless hysteresis rules trigger a change. This is what makes it a TREND radar (sectors evolve) rather than a fixed taxonomy. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if I had this earlier, we had only Models / RAG, and now from RAG we went to Agents, that's why I say it needs to be flexible.'
sector_config._clustering_method: LLM clusters topics into themes by reading topic labels + supporting context. Prior run's sectors are passed in as starting point — clusterer keeps them when membership is stable, splits/merges/renames only when warranted. The topic_taxonomy_seed group keys above are initial hints, NOT enforced labels.
sector_config._starter_sectors_comment: Used only on the very first radar run when no prior sectors exist. After that, the clusterer evolves them. If sectors get stuck for too long, manually clearing prior_sectors in the most recent radar JSON forces a fresh cluster.

breadth_config._comment: Cross-source breadth — orthogonal to the EMA-based persistence score. Answers 'how many distinct organizations are talking about this right now?' as a primary, visible dimension. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if many companies are talking or writing about the same topic, this means high-weighted related, should be seen easier.'
breadth_config._org_definition: An 'org' is the primary publisher or subject of the mention — Anthropic, OpenAI, ServiceNow, Heise, Handelsblatt, an individual author of a long-form blog post. The radar skill extracts orgs from each mention's context. For backfill where org data isn't separately stored, breadth is approximated by distinct (source_type, file_date) pairs in the window.

thresholds._comment: How the viewer interprets breadth into visual cues. Raised 2026-05-23: original 5/8 floor was below the natural median (14 today) so the high_breadth flag fired on every topic. New floor 15/20 ~= top-third / top-quartile of today's distribution. Re-tune if topic count grows past ~60 or the rolling median shifts.

max_mentions_per_source_type._comment: Per-source cap on counted mentions per topic per run. Prevents one chatty source (LinkedIn hashtags, Medium aggregators) from dominating the score just by volume. Beyond the cap, additional mentions are recorded in source_mentions for transparency but stop adding to raw_score. Tune up/down based on what dominates the radar — added 2026-05-12 after LinkedIn accounted for 46% of a topic's score.

stages._comment: Each topic falls into one stage based on score AND sustained signal. Tuning these thresholds shifts how aggressively the radar promotes/demotes themes.

emerging.description: Early signal. 1-2 weak sources or one strong novel source. Worth watching.

consolidating.description: Multiple independent sources are converging on the same take. Pattern is forming.

mainstream.description: Consensus. Most credible sources reference this; further coverage is incremental.

fading._trigger: score declined >25% over rolling window AND was previously >=50
fading.description: Was hot, now declining. Useful to know — don't bet here, expect coverage to dry up.
